key_insight: A wall’s leading-edge position changes near-wall bubble dynamics, shifting both the bouncing-to-escaping transition and the rebound frequency even at similar bubble and wall conditions.
engineering_relevance: For bubble-contacting equipment and wall-bounded multiphase flows, geometry and upstream bubble history must be considered alongside Bond, Galilei, Reynolds, and wall spacing to predict separation and escape behavior.
method: Compared rising deformable gas bubbles in ultrapure water near a vertical wall.
Tested two wall placements: one starting near the injector and one beginning downstream after the bubble reaches terminal velocity.
Mapped regimes and rebound dynamics using dimensionless groups (Bo, Ga, Re, St).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that downstream wall placement triggers bouncing-tumbling-escaping at smaller bubble sizes and lower Bo, Ga, and Re, while periodic-bouncing Strouhal numbers drop substantially versus the upstream-wall case.
watch_item: Results depend on a specific wall geometry and initial bubble hydrodynamic history, so direct transfer to other fluids, wall shapes, or injection conditions may be limited.
paper_title: Influence of a vertical-wall leading edge on bouncing and escape bubble rising regimes
